Demarcation

/dee-mar-KAY-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Demarcation means the marking of a clear boundary or dividing line between two things

Demarcation means the marking of a clear boundary or dividing line between two things. The surveyor drove bright orange stakes along the property line, and that demarcation finally ended the neighbors' argument over where one yard stopped and the other began.

Worked Example

The textbook uses the invention of the printing press as its demarcation between the medieval period and the early modern era.

Demarcation fits because the printing press serves as a clear dividing line between two categories of history — everything before it belongs to one era, everything after it to another, with the boundary explicitly marked.

How Demarcation Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

delineation

delineation: the precise outlining or describing of something's limits

boundary

boundary: a line that marks the limit of an area or category

borderline

borderline: the line marking where one thing ends and another begins

Antonyms

blurring

blurring: making a line or difference unclear

merging

merging: combining two things into one

How Strong Is It? — distinction → demarcation → gulf

distinction vs. demarcation

distinction vs. demarcation: A distinction is weaker — it notes a difference between two things without demarcation's sense of an explicitly drawn, marked-out line.

gulf vs. demarcation

gulf vs. demarcation: A gulf is stronger — it implies a vast, hard-to-bridge separation between two things, far beyond a line that has simply been drawn and labeled.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of demarcation.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: off, completely (Latin, here an intensifier)

Root — marc

Root — marc: boundary, boundary sign (ancient Germanic marka, which entered Romance languages as marcar, 'to mark')

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: the act or process of (noun-forming)

Put it together

Put it together: Demarcation is 'the act of marking off completely' — the ancient root marka named a physical boundary sign, so the word still pictures someone going along a line and planting markers to show exactly where one territory, category, or duty ends and the next begins.

Use the root in a new word: remark

Use the root in a new word: remark: The inspector jotted a quick remark about the loose stair railing before moving on to the next floor.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal / technical

Demarcation shows up in law, labor, geography, and formal writing — often in the set phrases 'line of demarcation' and 'demarcation dispute' (a labor term for arguments over which workers may do which jobs). In casual speech, people just say 'dividing line' or 'boundary.'
